title: Porajmos: Nazi Genocide of the Roma and Sinti
summary: Germany and its allies killed Roma and Sinti across Europe between 1939 and 1945: shot in the occupied Soviet Union, deported to ghettos and camps, and sent to Auschwitz. Historians estimate at least 250,000 dead, with some scholars proposing about 500,000. The Birkenau family camp was liquidated on the night of 2-3 August 1944.

uncertainty.note: The process spans 1939-1945 per the USHMM article title; start and end are year-level and the persecution did not begin or end on a single date.

where.modern_name: Auschwitz II-Birkenau, Oswiecim County, Poland (representative site; the genocide covered much of Europe)
where.historical_name: Auschwitz II-Birkenau, in German-annexed Upper Silesia, occupied Poland (section BIIe held the so-called Gypsy family camp)

importance.justification: A genocide of a European minority, long under-recognised, with victim estimates of 250,000 to about 500,000 per USHMM.

audience_note: Describes mass killing, including of children. Figures are historians' estimates and differ between sources.

sources.title: 79th anniversary of the liquidation of the Roma camp in Auschwitz

reviewer_note: Pin is Birkenau as a sourced representative site only; the process was continent-wide (shootings in the Soviet Union, Croatia, Romania deportations), hence the 2,500 km uncertainty. USHMM says about 23,000 Roma and Sinti were deported to Auschwitz with roughly 21,000 dying; the Auschwitz Museum says 21,000 were registered and 19,000 died, plus 2,000 unregistered. Birkenau liquidation toll: Museum about 4,300; USHMM 4,200-4,300. The term Porajmos was not on the opened pages.
